newsitem.title: UK: SWIMMING-FOUR CHINESE SWIMMERS TEST POSITIVE.
newsitem.headline: SWIMMING-FOUR CHINESE SWIMMERS TEST POSITIVE.

text.p: Four Chinese swimmers have been banned for two years after positive dope tests at the national championships in January last year.
Cornel Marculescu, director of the world governing body FINA, said in Lausanne on Tuesday that three women and one man had been suspended.
Women swimmer Yu Ran, Pu Shi and Chen Jialin tested positive for an anabolic steroid while Lu Qiang had an illegally high ratio of testosterone to epitestosterone.

Marculescu said China would not be suspended from international competition for two years under a rule passed at last year's Atlanta Olympics because the results had been reported by the Chinese federation.
A nation is suspended only if FINA testers catch the culprits.
Marculescu also said a year's delay in revealing the positive tests was not unusual.
"It's a matter of procedure," he said. "These cases take a long time."
The quartet are banned for two years only because the offences were committed before the four-year ban came into force.

Seven Chinese tested positive for anabolic steroids at the 1994 Asian Games a month after the world championships in Rome. World champions Yang Aihua and Lu Bin were among those suspended for two years.
